page: Amazon Web Services c7i-flex.16xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual machine delivered on the AWS Nitro System. It is powered by 4th Generation Intel Xeon Scalable processors (model 8488C) operating at a base frequency of 3.2 GHz across 32 physical cores and 64 vCPUs, configured with burstable CPU allocation. The instance features 105 MB of L3 cache, 2 MB of L2 cache per core, and support for hardware extensions including AVX-512, AMX (Advanced Matrix Extensions) for int8 and tile operations, and hardware cryptography acceleration via AES and SHA extensions.

The hardware configuration includes 128.0 GB of DDR5 memory running at 5000 MHz, providing a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio (2.0 GB per vCPU). The system provides 12 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. It contains no bundled local storage, requiring network-attached storage solutions for persistent data. The instance does not include discrete GPU hardware accelerators.

Benchmark evaluations reveal top-quartile results across memory bandwidth, cryptographic routines, vector-heavy calculations, and CPU-driven inference. Read-only memory bandwidth tests achieve 4,612.53 GB/sec in L1 cache and 200.81 GB/sec on uncached 256 MB blocks. Synthetic multi-threaded decompression reached 314.73 GB/sec in bzip3 tests, alongside high throughput in PassMark CPU extended instructions and encryption workloads. CPU-based machine learning inference is notably strong, achieving 2,620.28 tokens per second on prompt processing for 135M parameter models and 227.81 tokens per second on 7B models, accelerated by AMX support. General multi-core compute tests such as stress-ng and Geekbench multi-core place in the median range due to the burstable vCPU scheduling profile.

The instance delivers high compute resource density at a favorable cost-performance balance within the 64-vCPU tier, utilizing flexible scheduling rather than fixed continuous headroom. It is well matched for software compilation, high-throughput web serving, parallel batch data processing, Redis in-memory caches, and CPU-based lightweight machine learning inference.
description: Amazon Web Services c7i-flex.16xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor, utilizing 4th Generation Intel Xeon 8488C processors running at 3.2 GHz. The instance provisions 64 burstable vCPUs across 32 physical cores, 105 MB of L3 cache, and 128.0 GB of DDR5 system memory operating at 5000 MHz, establishing a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio. Local storage is omitted, and networking offers 12 Gbps of baseline bandwidth. Advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 and Intel AMX drive top-quartile execution in cryptographic tests, software compilation, database tasks, and CPU-based neural network inference. Burstable CPU allocation yields cost efficiency for variable compute requirements, although sustained maximum-load operations may see throttled CPU potential compared to non-flex tiers. Best-fit use cases include scalable web serving, CI/CD compilation pipelines, Redis caching clusters, and mid-tier batch data processing.
